terms.meaning: The living and non-living things together.
Karnataka's tree-hugging movement to save forests, like Chipko in the north.
The forest department's planting of exotic trees like Nilgiri and Acacia.
The measuring jar for crops whose size the Kagodu farmers protested in 1951.
The Karnataka dalit organisation formed under the Association of Dalit Writers and Artists; Prof. B. Krishnappa was its convenor.

items.name: Gandhiji on nature
items.formula: "Nature has enough for everybody's need, not everybody's greed."
items.example: Environmental movements reached Karnataka in the 1970s.

items.name: Fights over rivers and mines
items.formula: Sahyadri Mining Protest Forum against Kudremukh mining, which polluted the Bhadra.
items.example: Protests against Harihar Polyfibres polluting the Tungabhadra, and against mining in Ballari.

items.name: Chipko and Appiko
items.formula: Movements to protect trees; Sunderlal Bahuguna gave his life to Chipko.
items.example: Environmentalists opposed Nilgiri because it lowers groundwater.

items.name: Organic farming
items.example: Karnataka set up an Organic Farming Mission and leads the country.

items.name: Firsts for Karnataka women
items.formula: Srirangamma and Rukminamma were the first women with B.A. Honours.
items.example: Indiramma was the first woman Mayor of Bengaluru.

items.name: Reservation for women
items.formula: Karnataka was the first state to give women 50% of seats in local bodies.
items.example: Women have 33% of government jobs; 1975 was International Women's Year.

items.name: Kagodu agitation (1951)
items.formula: The first post-independence farmers' fight, in Shivamogga, against the Kolaga system.
items.example: Led by Shantaveri Gopala Gowda; Ram Manohar Lohia came to support it.

items.name: Malaprabha farmers' protest (1980)
items.formula: Cotton failed; more than 20 farmers of Navalgund, Naragund and Savadatti died in police firing.
items.example: Leaders of later farmers' groups: M. D. Nanjundaswamy, Sundaresh, Puttannaiah.

items.name: Early steps for dalits
items.formula: Chamaraja Wodeyar X opened schools for dalits after Vivekananda's visit.
items.example: In 1936 M. C. Raja led the first dalit entry into Mysore palace.

items.name: Watchwords of the dalit movement
items.formula: Education, organisation and agitation, inspired by Ambedkar, the "Dalit Surya".
items.example: B. Shyamsundar set up the Bhimasena Organisation in 1970.

items.name: Basavalingappa episode (1973)
items.formula: Minister Basavalingappa called Kannada literature "fodder"; the protests made him resign.
items.example: It raised dalit awareness; the Association of Dalit Writers and Artists formed at Bhadravati in 1976.

items.name: Dalit writers
items.formula: Devanuru Mahadeva and Dr. Siddalingaiah showed dalit life through their works.
items.example: Dalit writers now help shape their community's future.

items.name: Save Kannada movement
items.formula: In the 1960s, A. N. Krishna Rao, Chidanandamurthy, M. N. Ramamurthy and Vatal Nagaraj worked for Kannada in Bengaluru.
items.example: Groups: Karnataka Yuvajana Sabha, Kannada Jagruta Parishat, Kannada Shakti Kendra.

items.name: Gokak agitation (1982)
items.formula: The Gokak committee gave Kannada first place: 150 of the 350 marks in the three-language plan.
items.example: When the report wasn't accepted, Dr. Rajkumar led a statewide agitation, backed by Kuvempu.

mistakes.text: Chipko and Appiko are both tree-hugging movements; Bahuguna is linked with Chipko.
Local bodies: 50% for women. Government jobs: 33%.
Dr. V. K. Gokak chaired the committee; Dr. Rajkumar led the agitation for it.
